title: Accessibility UX-lint: ARIA semantics, token regression, and keyboard heuristics for Embedded Analytics kit
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Scope: Run a focused accessibility lint and remediation cycle across the Embedded Analytics component kit (compact table, mini-heatmap, sparkline, and action-pill buttons). Goal is to detect token regressions introduced by the recent compact density token migration, fix ARIA semantics for composite widgets, and implement explicit keyboard heuristics for dense interactions. Deliverables include a Figma update, token guidance, ARIA pattern snippets, and VPAT evidence attachments for audit teams.
acceptance_criteria: Compact control token contrast meets WCAG AA for normal text in both light and dark themes per automated tests and manual spot-checks
All composite widgets (table rows with inline actions, mini-heatmap, sparklines with tooltip triggers) expose correct ARIA roles and labels and pass the a11y regression checklist
Keyboard tab/arrow flow is documented and validated with a keyboard-only walkthrough script for each widget
Design assets (Figma) reflect updated tokens and have migration notes; token deltas called out in the PR description
VPAT evidence folder contains screenshots, test scripts, and a short findings summary ready for compliance review
design_notes: Initial hypothesis: compact density token shift lowered contrast on secondary interactive labels and altered focus ring thickness. Proposed remediation: reintroduce a secondary contrast ramp for small text, increase focus ring stroke on small actionable pills, and add explicit aria-describedby for chart tooltips that are keyboard-triggerable. Prefer minimal visual change while meeting AA.
